content: coffee A controlled blast on a movie set close to the O2 venue in London ignited a fire that consumed a van and caused damage to a car and a lorry. Fire crews were dispatched to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown shortly before eight o’clock on Saturday. After a little more than an hour the flames were brought under control thanks to the efforts of several firefighters, and no one was hurt. Authorities said the blaze stemmed from a pre‑arranged filming activity near the O2 arena, which is slated to host shows by Niall Horan and Texas in the coming days. The London Fire Brigade updated on X that evening, noting that the fire at the Silvertown yard was now contained, that a van had been destroyed while most of a car and a lorry suffered damage, and that there were no injury reports. They added that the fire originated from a controlled explosion on the set that escaped containment, that crews acted swiftly to put it out and would stay on site for the rest of the evening. The yard lies near the Thames cable‑car crossing, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman confirmed they were aware of reports of explosions heard near the O2 in Greenwich.
